newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pakistan buys mogas at plus $25.43/T from Hascombe.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan buys mogas at plus $25.43/T from Hascombe.

text.p: Pakistan's Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Resources said on Monday it has awarded its tender to buy 50,000 tonnes of 80-octane leaded gasoline at $25.43 per tonne over Mideast naphtha spot quotes to U.K.-based trading company Hascombe.
The award, on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Pakistan, was for two 25,000-tonne cargoes for delivery in the first and last weeks of May, an official said.
The tender which closed on March 31 and was valid until April 5, was actually awarded on April 1, he said.
"When we scrapped the tender in early March, the offer was $7.50 higher than this award," he said.

The ministry usually makes its imports purchases through quarterly tenders across the barrel, but had issued a separate gasoline tender after receiving high offers in its original tender for second quarter requirements.

Pakistan received offers of around $30 per tonne over Mideast naphtha quotes c-and-f for the cancelled second quarter tender--nearly double the $16.745 premium it paid Hascombe for its first quarter purchases, sources said.
Pakistan doubled its May purchases to two cargoes due to the scheduled shutdown of the state-owned National Refining Ltd's 63,000-barrel-per-day refinery for 20-days from April 25, the official said.
